messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate and increased P95 latency observed for Hosted API and several Dedicated pools in eu-west-1. Detected by edge-proxy and dedicated-pool telemetry. Auto-pager triggered.

elena (oncall): Ack. I'm on pager, starting triage. Observability shows a sharp rise in STS/ELB errors around 2026-03-15T22:14:12Z.

chris: I'm joining. Can you paste the first failing log lines / metrics?

elena (oncall): Quick metrics snapshot:
```
edge-proxy:euw1 5xx_rate = 12.4% (baseline 0.3%)
dedicated-pool-g3:euw1 latency_p95 = 1.8s (baseline 200ms)
api-gateway:euw1 errors = 503, 504, 502 spike
sts-call-failures = 28% of calls
```
Looks correlated with AWS STS STS throttling and ELB 5xx for region.

sam (sre): We're also seeing retries increasing token-exchange timeouts. Root cause looks like third-party (AWS regional) auth/service egress issues.

maria (eng): Is hosted traffic failing-over to other regions automatically? What are our routing fallbacks right now?

elena (oncall): We have routing policy: prefer eu-west-1, fallback to eu-west-3 then to us-east-1 for non-data-sovereign customers. Fallback not fully triggered because a number of requests were sticky due to KV cache affinity.

chris: Immediate mitigations: 1) enable cross-region fallback for auth calls (force failover) 2) scale dedicated pool buffer by +2 nodes 3) reduce batch size for interactive routes to lower tail latency.

elena (oncall): Applying 1 and 3 now. Running command to flip auth egress routing:
```
# run from infra admin
redwoodctl routing set auth-egress --region eu-west-1 --fallback eu-west-3 --force
```
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: routing-change v2026.03.15.1 by elena (oncall) — started.

nathan (cust-succ): Heads up: customer-facing dashboards show increased 502/503 for some high-traffic customer apps (acme-corp, finlytics, chatflow). I'm drafting an outgoing status note. Any ETA?

elena (oncall): No ETA yet. Waiting for routing flip to propagate and for STS error rates to drop. If auth calls continue to fail post-failover, we'll enable model-variant fallback to a lower-QPS token cache mode.

sam (sre): I've scaled dedicated pools: added 2 nodes to eu-west-1 dedicated pools (g3). Also applied temporary NLB connection timeout bump to avoid mid-request terminations. Commands run:
```
redwoodctl pools scale dedicated-euw1-g3 +2
redwoodctl nlb set timeout eu-west-1 120s
```

maria (eng): Reduced batch size for chat endpoints to 1 for latency-sensitive routes and turned off auto-batching for the next 20m.

elena (oncall): Routing-change finished: all auth egress traffic now preferentially goes to eu-west-3. Observability: STS call error rate dropped from 28% -> 6% in the last 3m. Edge 5xx rate down to 4.1% (still above baseline).

chris: Good. Continue monitoring. If errors don't fall under 1% within 10m, consider enabling static token cache mode for hosted customers (risk: stale tokens for short window).

nathan (cust-succ): Draft status (sending to #status-notifications for review):
"We are investigating elevated errors and latency in our eu-west-1 region affecting Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Traffic is being routed to eu-west-3 as a mitigation. Some customers may see transient 5xx responses. We will provide updates every 15 minutes"

elena (oncall): 👍 send that. Also add note that we are not seeing data loss and requests are eventually succeeding for the majority.

chris: Observability callout: downstream ELB 5xx traces still visible for a subset of frontends. I'm opening a ticket with AWS support (case 123456789) for eu-west-1 ELB/STS region issues.

sam (sre): Customer impact matrix so far:
- acme-corp: elevated 503, retried and largely recovered after failover (approx 9% failed requests end-user visible)
- finlytics: streaming sessions experienced reconnects, some token refresh failures (approx 12% error budget consumed)
- chatflow: short spikes of 504s on long completions >8s (we reduced batching)

maria (eng): We should schedule a canary check for Dedicated pools to ensure model responses are correct after failover. I'll run test prompts against a dedicated instance.

elena (oncall): Handoff plan: I'm staying on pager for another 30m; if this stabilizes I'll hand to chris for the midnight shift. chris you ready to take full ownership at 23:00 UTC?

chris: I can take it. If things degrade again I'll escalate to infra lead.

deploy-bot: routing-change v2026.03.15.1 completed — all health checks passed.

elena (oncall): Observability update 22:38 UTC: edge 5xx = 2.2%, p95 latency dropped to 420ms. STS failures at 3.1%. Continuing to watch.

nathan (cust-succ): Sent status update to affected customers and posted to public status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/3412345678. Keeping them informed.

maria (eng): Post-mortem action items (quick list):
- Improve sticky affinity fallback so KV cache affinity doesn't prevent region failover
- Add automated health-check-triggered auth-egress failover rule (threshold-based)
- Consider cached token mode for high-error windows
- Improve observability alerts to include STS/ELB correlations

sam (sre): Agreed. Also recommend a runbook update for dedicated pool scale-up steps (include exact redwoodctl commands).

elena (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated for now. Will keep thread open during handoff. Switching to watch-mode.

chris: Taking over at 23:00 UTC. If anything pops back up, @elena please ping.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. Next update in 30m or on-change.

elena (oncall): Thanks team. I'll write the incident timeline in #postmortems once we confirm full recovery.

chris: Note for postmortem: dependency risk — STS/ELB regional degradations; consider multi-region auth pools.

nathan (cust-succ): Closing customer comms loop after next stability confirmation.

(ended by chris)
